quote: The current tests are with a 10 mm thick PMMA slab in support of the Saffire II sample 9 test [15].
subject: Ground tests on the same 10 mm PMMA slab as Saffire-II sample 9

quote: Results show that reductions of pressure slow down the flame spread over the PMMA surface approaching that in microgravity.
subject: Thick PMMA, concurrent flow: lowering the pressure on the ground slows flame spread toward the spread in orbit
conditions: Ground: 100 to 40 kPa, 200 mm/s forced flow. Orbit: Saffire-II, 100 kPa, 200 mm/s (same abstract).

quote: The extrapolation of the correlation to low pressures predicts well the flame spread rate obtained in microgravity in the Saffire II experiments.
subject: A mixed-convection correlation of the ground data, carried to low pressure, predicts the Saffire-II spread rate

quote: it would be necessary to reduce the pressure to values of the order of 30 to 20 kPa to simulate microgravity conditions
subject: To imitate microgravity on the ground, the pressure would have to fall to about 20 to 30 kPa
conditions: Thick PMMA in concurrent flow; the authors add that some simplifications of their analysis may not hold there.

quote: As ambient pressure is progressively reduced, the flame spread characteristics get closer to what is observed in microgravity.
subject: Concluding remark: at lower pressure the flame looks and spreads more like the flame in orbit

quote: The spacecraft ventilation system induces flows with velocities that are of the order 100 mm/s to 200 mm/s, while the buoyant flow induced by a propagating flame have velocities of the order of 300 mm/s to 600 mm/s.
subject: Why ground tests cannot copy a spacecraft fire: cabin air moves at 100 to 200 mm/s, a flame's own buoyant flow on Earth at 300 to 600 mm/s

quote: Results were convincing although rather anticlimactic as none of the silicone samples burned.
subject: No Saffire-II silicone sample burned in orbit
conditions: Silicone 0.27, 0.61, 1.03 mm (concurrent) and 0.37 mm (opposed), 20 cm/s, about 22.1% O2.

quote: It was surprising that not even the thin sample could permit any flame spread, given that it was entirely consumed in normal gravity.
subject: The thinnest silicone burned completely at 1 g but did not spread in orbit

quote: ‒ The 0.27-mm thick samples were almost always completely consumed
subject: Silicone 0.27 mm, upward at 1 g: almost always completely consumed
conditions: NASA's normal-gravity upward-burning tests of the Saffire-II silicone thicknesses.

quote: ‒ The 0.61-mm thickness burned on average 7.6 cm of the available 30 cm before extinguishing
subject: Silicone 0.61 mm, upward at 1 g: average burn length
conditions: NASA's normal-gravity upward-burning tests; the 1 g sample length is given here as 30 cm.

quote: ‒ The 1.03-mm thickness would not burn at all.
subject: Silicone 1.03 mm, upward at 1 g: would not burn

quote: In downward burning, normal gravity tests, this thickness was completely consumed. The next higher thickness tested (0.61 mm) would not burn.
subject: Silicone 0.37 mm, downward at 1 g: completely consumed; 0.61 mm would not burn

quote: Flammability of silicone in microgravity appears to be reduced compared to normal gravity, at least for the flow speeds tested.
